summary: Stand aside on BTC/USDT until after the US October CPI release at 13:30 UTC today, about 2h20m away and inside both sides' 4-8 hour window. The debate is a near-draw (28 vs 29): the bull's revised long pays a real 1.8R to VWAP, and the bear's short has a valid plan but has not triggered. Re-assess after the print: a reclaim of VWAP near 74,736 favours longs, and a 1h close below 74,091 favours shorts.
reasoning:
Two facts decide this. First, the BLS schedule confirms October 2026 CPI is released today, Nov 10, at 8:30 ET (13:30 UTC). That is about 2h20m after the re-check and inside the 4-8 hour window both sides proposed. Under the rules, a major scheduled event inside the trade window means NO TRADE. Both debaters accepted the risk ('do not add into the print', 'flat or half size through CPI'), which concedes that neither plan survives the event cleanly. Second, the scores are within 3 points (bull 28, bear 29).

The bull's best work was in Round 3. The bull replaced the 700-point stop with 73,900, below the 24h low of 74,091.64 and the 5m low of 74,115.65. From 74,200 that is 300 of risk against about 536 to VWAP (74,736.41 now) and about 1,185 to the 1h upper band (75,385.52), so the 1.8R and 4.0R figures check out on live data. The bear's Round 3 still attacked the old 0.84R plan and never answered the revised one. That is a real gap in the bear's rebuttal. However, a 300-point stop is only 0.7x the 1h ATR (427) and sits in front of a CPI print that CoinDesk says is being traded on December-hike pricing. Slippage through it is likely.

The bear's macro claims are verified. The Block confirms the -$1.28B ETF week, YTD -$914.1M, and the daily flows. CoinDesk's markets page carries the rate-hike and CPI headlines and the Waller line. The bear's structure claims (below the SMA200 on all frames, 1h MACD histogram deepening to -56.4) remain true. The bear's 0.17 order-book reading was a transient print, which the bear later withdrew; the live book now reads 0.37. The bear's short entry zone of 74,450-74,650 has not been reached (price 74,317), so there is no live short to take either.

trade_plan.entry: No position before the 13:30 UTC CPI release. After the print, a long is only valid on a 15m close back above VWAP (about 74,736) and the 1h EMA21 (about 74,744). A short is only valid on a 1h close below 74,091 (24h low) on rising volume, or on a rejection of 74,450-74,650 after the print.
trade_plan.stop_loss: n/a. If either post-CPI setup triggers, place the stop beyond the level that triggered it, at least 1x the 15m ATR (about 190) away.
trade_plan.risk_reward: n/a. Require at least 1.5R to a real level before acting after the print.
trade_plan.timeframe: Re-evaluate from 13:45 UTC, once the CPI candle has closed.
trade_plan.risk_rule: Risk no more than 1% of trading capital on this idea.

invalidation: This stand-aside is wrong only if BTC trends cleanly before 13:30 UTC (a 1h close above 74,744 or below 74,091) without reversing on the CPI print. Even then, entering into the release is not justified under the rules.
key_risks: US October CPI at 13:30 UTC today, with CoinDesk reporting December-hike pricing; expect a gap move that can skip tight stops (1h ATR about 427).
Trend is down on every timeframe (price below the SMA200 on 5m/15m/1h; 1h MACD histogram -56.4), so bounces may fail at VWAP and the 1h EMA21 near 74,740.
Spot ETF outflows of -$1.28B last week (YTD -$914M) could continue in today's US session.
The order book's top-100 ratio swings between 0.17 and 2.54 within minutes and is not a reliable signal either way.
